severity_criteria.source_excerpt: Trial Population and inclusion criteria: "moderate-to-severe AD for at least 1 year, defined according to the Hanifin and Rajka Criteria," "2 an EASI score of ≥16, an IGA score of ≥3 and a body surface area (BSA) affected by AD of" "≥10% will be enrolled (adolescent patients aged ≥12 to <18 years will make up 12.5% of the" "EASI score ≥16 at the Baseline Visit" "IGA score ≥3 (moderate) (scale of 0 [clear] to 4 [severe]) at the Baseline visit" "≥10% BSA of AD involvement at the Baseline visit" -- The protocol eligibility text identifies the population as moderate-to-severe and gives baseline EASI, IGA, and affected BSA thresholds. IGA 3 is explicitly called moderate and uses the stated 0-to-4 scale.

prohibited_concomitant: Systemic corticosteroids for treatment of atopic dermatitis
Introduction of medications or therapies for other medical conditions known to affect atopic dermatitis
permitted_concomitant: Medications for other medical conditions (e.g., hypertension, diabetes, acute infections)
Acute infections may be treated with systemic antibiotics
value.population_note: All patients used concomitant TCS. Mid-potency TCS was applied at least once daily until lesions were clear/almost clear, then switched to low potency for seven days and stopped; low potency could replace mid potency on thin skin/atrophic areas. After Week 16, TCS use was at investigator discretion.

background_therapy.source_excerpt: Table 6, Concomitant Medications; sections 7.1, 9.9.2 and 9.9.3: "All enrolled patients are required to start treatment with mid- or low-potency TCS at Baseline" "TCS All patients must use concomitant TCS." "patients will apply mid-potency TCS and low-potency TCS." "Medium-potency TCS should be applied at least once daily to" "Patients should then switch to low-potency TCS and treat" "Low-potency TCS may be used from the Baseline visit in place of" "From Week 16 to Week 52, TCS use will be at Investigator" "triamcinolone acetonide 0.1% cream, and a low-potency TCS, hydrocortisone 1% cream (for" " The use of systemic corticosteroids for the treatment of AD is prohibited and requires" "permanent discontinuation of the Investigational Product." " Cannabinoid treatments for AD are prohibited." "The introduction of medications or therapies for other medical conditions known to have an" "effect on AD are not permitted during the study." "The dosing regimen of a 500 mg loading dose at Baseline and Week 2, followed by 250 mg of" "given at Baseline and Week 2, and at Week 16 and Week 18 during the Maintenance Period" -- The study is explicitly lebrikizumab plus required TCS. The protocol gives step-down and recurrence instructions but the schema’s step_down_rule requires an unsupported toxicity-stop boolean, so the regimen subtype and nested rule remain null. Treatment-period restrictions are drawn from Section 9.9.3; the separate one-week pre-Baseline TCS restriction is not treated as a concomitant prohibition.

multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: Statistical Hypotheses and 11.11 Multiplicity Strategy: " H1: PLebrikizumab – Pplacebo ≠ 0," "where PLebrikizumab refers to the proportion of patients receiving lebrikizumab, and Pplacebo refers" "No control for multiplicity between the primary and secondary variables will be taken into" "account." "Please see Section 11.8.1.1 for the strategy of analysis for the primary and key" "procedure will thus be 2-sided." -- The confirmatory primary hypothesis is two-sided. The protocol explicitly says no multiplicity control is applied between primary and secondary variables, so familywise control across that group is false. The analysis-method references do not establish a fixed testing sequence, and the protocol states no specific hierarchy.

value.source_inconsistency: SAP v2.0 gives the core trial as 72 weeks overall, with up to 4 weeks of screening, 52 weeks of treatment (last dose at Week 50), and an 18-week post-last-dose safety follow-up. Its Germany amendment adds an extension beginning at Week 52 or within 8 weeks after the Week 50 dose, lasting at least 24 weeks and continuing until lebrikizumab is commercially available; extension participants have a safety follow-up 4 weeks after their final dose. These are population-specific schedules, so one fixed study end and follow-up duration cannot represent both.

value.applies_to_period: During the trial; no earliest week specified
value.rationale: If medically necessary, high-potency TCS or systemic treatment (e.g. oral corticosteroids or phototherapy) may be used. High-potency TCS users continue lebrikizumab and scheduled visits; systemic rescue requires permanent study-drug discontinuation. No quantitative trigger threshold is stated.

rescue_therapy.source_excerpt: 9.9.4 Rescue Treatment for Atopic Dermatitis and 8.3.2 Study Drug Discontinuation: "If medically necessary (eg, to control intolerable AD symptoms), high-potency TCS or" "systemic treatments (eg, oral corticosteroids, phototherapy) may be used." "Patients using high-potency TCS will continue treatment with lebrikizumab and should" "continue to attend all study visits and be assessed for safety and efficacy according to the SoA." "Study drug must be permanently discontinued for patients receiving systemic rescue treatment" "as outlined in Section 9.9.3." -- The protocol describes medically necessary rescue at investigator discretion, distinguishes topical high-potency rescue from systemic rescue, and states the consequences for study drug and visits. No numeric trigger or timing threshold is supplied.
